source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
The booklet gives a fertilizer application timetable for watermelon with three columns: timing, fertilizer type and amount, and where to place it.

Base application, about 15 days before transplanting: organic fertilizer (well-decomposed animal manure or compost) at about 2 kilograms per meter of bed length, buried into the soil while preparing the bed/ridge.

Base application, about 3 to 5 days before transplanting: NPK 20-20-0 or 15-15-15 at about 5 grams per planting hole, placed in the hole mixed with soil at roughly 3 centimeters depth.

7 days after transplanting: urea (46-0-0) at about 1.5 grams per plant, placed in two small holes about 8 centimeters from the base of the plant.

15 days after transplanting: NPK 20-20-0 or 15-15-15 at about 5 grams per plant, placed in two holes about 15 centimeters from the base of the plant.

25 days after transplanting: NPK 20-20-0 or 15-15-15 at about 5 grams per plant, placed in two holes about 25 centimeters from the base of the plant.

35 days after transplanting: NPK 20-20-0 at about 5 grams per plant together with potassium fertilizer (0-0-60) at about 5 grams per plant, placed in two holes about 25 centimeters from the base of the plant.

45 days after transplanting: potassium fertilizer (0-0-60) at about 9 grams per plant, placed in two holes about 25 centimeters from the base of the plant.

General guidance: watermelon needs enough fertilizer suited to the crop's growth stage; farmers should apply fertilizer that matches local field conditions.
